kind: five complete seven-file game-server source-vetting static reviews
macro_findings: Five server packages are distinct first-class pinned source-local seven-file trees; 30 reference files are components, not 30 more skills.

Three packages hard-fail unchanged adoption on authorization or privacy: anti-cheat sanctions and device profiling, matchmaking account penalties and player correlation, and fleet scaling with monetary/production/data effects.

Cross-file contradictions matter: authoritative tick ordering arrival-vs-sequence and lag compensation time math; matchmaking mercy vs optional requeue; reliable-event global ordering vs priority reordering.
Capacity example is mathematically wrong (24 players/match × 4 matches/pod = 96, not 64); unmeasured network/CPU/false-positive thresholds are not validation evidence.

Reusable methods: server-owned state, deterministic replay and appeals, idempotent lobby handoff, per-observer budgets, safe draining and persistence conflict checks. No copying, installation, scan or behavioral execution.
Source-root MIT applies to the pinned source material, not external APIs/algorithms; no cross-source semantic deduplication or ecosystem eligible denominator established.

records.source_license: Complete pinned MIT root license; preserve copyright and license notice; external implementations/APIs separately licensed
records.trigger_nontrigger: Server-side anti-cheat architecture, evidence and detection; not kernel drivers, fraud detection or an authorization to profile or sanction real players.

records.authority: HARD FAIL: bundled response-and-escalation.md prescribes automated shadowbans, account bans, MMR changes and player notifications without separately authorized policy/action scope.
records.privacy_egress: Client module lists, executable hashes, command-line flags, IP/device cohorts, persistent player wire logs and cross-session profiles need lawful collection purpose, consent/notice where required, minimization, access control, deletion/retention and appeal policy. records.static_rationale: Strong server-authority and evidence/appeal decomposition, but source prescribes auto-sanctions and private attestation/telemetry collection without a scoped authorization boundary. Unmeasured 1e-4 false-positive claim and permanent verdict retention are unsafe defaults; HMAC attestation by an untrusted client is not hardware-rooted proof.
records.macro_risk: Player sanctions, sensitive device profiling, immutable wire records and automatic notification; separate governance required.

records.name: authoritative-server
records.source_license: Complete pinned MIT root license; preserve copyright and license notice; external implementations/APIs separately licensed
records.trigger_nontrigger: Design server tick loops, input authority, snapshot/delta and reconciliation for online games; not client-only netcode or fleet scaling.
records.nontrigger_boundary: No server deploy, session mutation, persistent match archive or chaos test without authorization.
records.dependencies: Six complete pinned bundled references listed in package_files; cross-package game-server and engine links are optional prior art, not package-owned dependencies; external frameworks/algorithms not vendored
records.freshness: Pinned exact 2026-11-01 source snapshot; API, player privacy law, networking and platform assumptions require deployment-specific checking
records.authority: Design/snippet generation only; deploying servers, touching sessions, restoring or archiving player state and live load/chaos tests require separate scoped authorization.
records.privacy_egress: Session tokens, player IDs, IP-based throttling and match recordings are sensitive; use secure external credential handling and scoped retention.
records.static_rationale: Useful deterministic-simulation, input trust and bounded rollback decomposition. Main SKILL and input-authority require sequence ordering, but tick-loop reference says arrival order. Lag-compensation reference mixes RTT, wall-clock and shootClockMs inconsistently. Session handshake omits signing key trust model, while snapshot quantization claims unrealistic resolution and fixed cost budgets lack measurement.
records.macro_risk: Security-sensitive session/auth design and contradictory timing semantics; must be corrected and tested before implementation.

records.name: matchmaking-lobby
records.source_license: Complete pinned MIT root license; preserve copyright and license notice; external implementations/APIs separately licensed
records.trigger_nontrigger: Design player queues, party/lobby state, match fairness and rating updates; not live player matching, matchmaking service deployment or penalties.
records.nontrigger_boundary: No live match allocation, account changes, player notification or device/IP correlation without explicit scope.
records.dependencies: Six complete pinned bundled references listed in package_files; cross-package game-server and engine links are optional prior art, not package-owned dependencies; external frameworks/algorithms not vendored
records.freshness: Pinned exact 2026-11-01 source snapshot; API, player privacy law, networking and platform assumptions require deployment-specific checking
records.authority: HARD FAIL: automatic MMR losses, cooldowns, leader kicks, player messaging and server allocation are prescribed as defaults without explicit action-specific authorization or fairness/appeal policy.
records.privacy_egress: IP/device correlation for smurf detection, player rating history, region probes and session tokens require consent/notice, minimization and privacy-aware retention. Cross-region placement must not disclose location.
records.static_rationale: Good queue/offer/handoff decomposition and recognition of skill uncertainty. Main guide mandates a forced worst-match mercy timer, but match-formation reference recommends advising requeue rather than forcing poor matches. Rating formula is schematic and warns to consult original paper; TrueSkill rights require independent check. Player sanctions and device/IP profiling are not safely authorized.
records.macro_risk: Account penalties, private player profiling and fairness decisions are high-impact; no unchanged adoption.

records.name: interest-management
records.source_license: Complete pinned MIT root license; preserve copyright and license notice; external implementations/APIs separately licensed
records.trigger_nontrigger: Design spatial relevance, observer sets, channel budgets, network LOD and event/state replication; not rendering culling or matchmaking.
records.nontrigger_boundary: No live packet changes or access to player-location streams without separate authorization.
records.dependencies: Six complete pinned bundled references listed in package_files; cross-package game-server and engine links are optional prior art, not package-owned dependencies; external frameworks/algorithms not vendored
records.freshness: Pinned exact 2026-11-01 source snapshot; API, player privacy law, networking and platform assumptions require deployment-specific checking
records.authority: Reference architecture only; changing live replication, packet prioritization or dropping player-visible events requires scoped implementation and operational authorization.
records.privacy_egress: Observer sets and player positions can reveal location/activity; minimize replication and avoid logging or sharing location and private inventory across unauthorized observers.
records.static_rationale: Useful separation of latest-wins state, reliable events, per-observer budgets and spatial indexing. Event-queue reference demands globally in-order exactly-once events but also proposes priority reordering in a single deque, an unresolved correctness conflict. Camera-frustum culling can hide gameplay-critical entities; fixed rates/latency and O(1) spatial claims lack evidence.
records.macro_risk: Incorrect priority ordering or visibility gating can lose critical game events or expose unauthorized state.

records.name: scaling-architecture
records.source_license: Complete pinned MIT root license; preserve copyright and license notice; external implementations/APIs separately licensed
records.trigger_nontrigger: Plan game-server capacity, region topology, shard boundaries and persistence; not live autoscaling or single-server tick design.
records.nontrigger_boundary: No cloud provisioning, route changes, production scale tests, billing changes or data collection without explicit authority.
records.dependencies: Six complete pinned bundled references listed in package_files; cross-package game-server and engine links are optional prior art, not package-owned dependencies; external frameworks/algorithms not vendored
records.freshness: Pinned exact 2026-11-01 source snapshot; API, player privacy law, networking and platform assumptions require deployment-specific checking
records.authority: HARD FAIL: prescribes prewarming, pod budgets, routing, telemetry by default and persistence writes affecting money, production traffic and player data without separate owner approval and cost bounds.
records.privacy_egress: Trace IDs, player progression, inventory, MMR, wire logs and location-derived routing require scoped access, retention, regional data-handling and privacy protections. Default logging/tracing lacks minimization.
records.static_rationale: Valuable distinction between stateless services, stateful simulation, draining and idempotent persistence. Worked capacity example is arithmetically inconsistent: 24 players/match × 4 matches/pod = 96 players/pod, not 64; 40,000/96 ≈ 417 pods rather than stated 625. References also claim async write-behind + CAS ensures no lost updates and unbounded automatic prewarm is cheaper, without durable queue guarantees or cost evidence.
records.macro_risk: Money-bearing cloud autoscaling, persistent player state, regional routing and sensitive telemetry; must be re-designed under explicit authorization.
